claim: Loss-of-function variants in TLR7 were identified in two families in which COVID-19 segregates like an X-linked recessive disorder environmentally conditioned by SARS-CoV-2.

claim: TLR7 deleterious variants were found in 2.1% of severely affected males and in none of the asymptomatic participants.

claim: Gender may influence COVID-19 disease outcome.

claim: Rare variants in the interferon type I pathway are responsible for inborn errors of immunity in a small proportion of patients.
source: Recent evidence suggests a fundamental role of interferon genes in modulating immunity to SARS-CoV-2; in particular, rare variants have recently been identified in the interferon type I pathway that are responsible for inborn errors of immunity in a small proportion of patients and auto-antibodies against type I interferon genes in up to 10% of severe COVID-19 cases (Zhang et al., 2020; Bastard et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2020 and Bastard et al., 2020.

claim: Auto-antibodies against type I interferon genes are found in up to 10% of severe COVID-19 cases.

claim: No rare TLR7 missense variants predicted to impact on protein function were found in any of the 77 SARS-CoV2 infected oligo-asymptomatic male participants.

claim: A TLR7 variant was found in one of 56 cases (1.7%) and in none of 27 controls in a similar cohort from the Italian second wave composed of male patients under 60 years of age without comorbidities.

All participants were white European. We found a TLR7 variant in one of 56 cases (1.7%) and in none of 27 controls.

claim: The association between the presence of TLR7 rare variants and severe COVID-19 was significant (p=0.037 by Fisher Exact test).
source: Overall, the association between the presence of TLR7 rare variants and severe COVID-19 was significant (p=0.037 by Fisher Exact test, Table 1).

claim: TLR7 rare missense variants were found in three additional patients over 60 years of age in the entire male cohort of 561 COVID-19 patients, including two cases (who shared the p.Ala1032Thr variant) and one control (C1), bearing the p.Val222Asp variant.

We found TLR7 rare missense variants in three additional patients over 60 years of age, including two cases (who shared the p.Ala1032Thr variant) and one control (C1), bearing the p.Val222Asp variant, predicted to have a low impact on protein function (CADD of 5.36) (Table 2).
